questions.prompt: After generating `jwt_private.pem` and `jwt_public.pem`, how should each be handled?
options: Commit both to source control so every developer has the same keys
Keep the public key secret and share the private key with each resource server
Store the private key where only the auth server process can read it; distribute the public key to resource servers
Reuse the dev key pair in production so tokens stay valid
questions.explanation: The private key signs tokens and belongs in a mounted secret or a vault. The public key only validates, so it can be shared more freely. Dev keys should not be reused in production, and `*.pem` goes in `.gitignore`.

questions.prompt: Why must the `Member` role be seeded before registration works?
options: Because `RegisterAsync` assigns the `"Member"` role by default
Because the migration fails without it
Because the JWT bearer scheme reads roles at startup
questions.explanation: The module's `RegisterAsync` puts every new user in `"Member"`, so that role (and any others your app uses, such as `Admin`) has to exist first.

questions.prompt: Which of the module's endpoints requires the caller to already be authenticated?
questions.explanation: Revoke (logout) requires auth. Register and login are entry points, and refresh takes the refresh token in the body instead of an access token.

questions.prompt: How should your existing task endpoints get the current user once the module is wired in?
options: Parse the `Authorization` header manually in each action
Read it through `ICurrentUserService`, so Application handlers stay testable without a web host
Read `HttpContext` directly inside the Application layer handlers
questions.explanation: The controllers just need `[Authorize]`. Reading the user via `ICurrentUserService` rather than touching `HttpContext` keeps the Application layer free of web dependencies.
